node.title: Re: Sometimes undef is initialized and sometimes not when hash values are fed to grep
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I'm pretty sure the answer is the same as in your previous [id://11110437|thread] that you referenced: map is providing lvalue context to its args, while the other two examples of string concatenation do not, hence the hash value is autovivified. (Update: I added [LanX]'s [id://11112782|suggested] workaround to the following example).

$ perl -wMstrict -MData::Dump -e 'my %h; map{$_} $h{X},"$h{Y}"; dd\%h' Use of uninitialized value $h{"Y"} in string at -e line 1. { X => undef }

See also your previous thread [id://1171041].

I'm curious why you have so many issues with autovivification? Personally, I hardly ever do, because I use [doc://exists], or [doc://keys] when looping over multiple hash keys. And if I have a situation where I want to control which keys can be accessed, I use locked hashes from [doc://Hash::Util].
